title: Execute the actual Gaussian RHS with a charged two-column physical kernel
body:
The actual Gaussian first-pass caller supplies real and imaginary RHS columns. The padded inverse-block consumer nevertheless computes all B columns. This package adds a physical two-column kernel that checks inactive inputs, preserves the original active-term order and rounding, and emits the complete padded output. B≤2 delegates to the original kernel.

The source-relative proof gives the zero-column invariant and complete local arithmetic/movement tariff. For B>2, the complete scalar count falls from 2(2K−1)B³ to 4(2K−1)B². The actual-Core B=4 fixture lowers complete consumer reads/writes/unit moves from 7,017,713 to 4,200,707 and retained owner backing from 9,953 to 9,731 cells. Exact padded output, protected tapes and same-owner reuse agree. The cross-block B4 case lowers total work from 21,413,925 to 12,862,809 and backing from 13,697 to 13,511 cells. B1/B2 preserve output with small dispatch overhead; no saving is claimed there.

Validation: normal four-case execution passed in 16.176s; the final committed Git-free export passed optimized full typed-receipt replay in 16.601s. Committed bytes/source history (33 files), explicit-input export integrity, package metadata and four actual CLI source-binding rejection controls pass. Independent optimized B4 replay and six physical controls also pass. The larger fixture tests a nonzero cross-block dependency; B1/B2 test fallback. Retained/adapted PR5483 helper hashes are authenticated separately, with predecessor attribution and self-contained runtime bytes.

This is a scoped ordinary arithmetic improvement, not a recursive paid-profile or κ improvement. LU(round_P(S)) is the supplied factor reference; no equivalence with the scalar BandedSolve rounding contract or complete normalized Core integration is claimed. Owned scratch retains the original blank-entry premise; arbitrary disjoint dirty spectators are preserved.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4182#discussioncomment-19173186

JoyboyBrian, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0 and predecessor attribution retained.
